title: The Line the Capital Didn't Print

lines.dialogue: Before dawn on the school veranda; the pond is black, the first lamps still lit.

Teacher Lek. Phum's boy died in the night. The death must be registered before the body is moved — and his rice sack is already on the platform. Once the bell rings, the tax falls due on a field one pair of hands short.
lines.stage_directions: sets his file case on the rail

lines.dialogue: A file case full of other people's names, and still the dead arrive before the ink.
lines.stage_directions: opens the tin box

lines.dialogue: Notebook. Pen. Carbon. Ink. Grief deserves a clean page.
lines.stage_directions: takes up his word-notebook, a reed pen, the carbon paper, the school's second inkstone — regarding each before choosing it

lines.dialogue: The circle murmurs condolences, low.
I can barely hear you — but I hear it.
lines.stage_directions: leans toward the circle

lines.dialogue: The motorcycle would not start in the damp. I walked.
I have seen it before — a death and a tax arriving in the same hour.
lines.stage_directions: to the circle

lines.dialogue: The register opens at dawn.
lines.stage_directions: checks his watch against the sky

lines.dialogue: The first paddy-birds cross the pond, going toward the fields.

line.dialogue: The register opens at dawn. Do we walk to the counter now, or wait for the family to ask for me?

choices.description: I will walk with him now and read the registration aloud for the family.

line.dialogue: I see the Officer open his file case to a clean page.
I see him check his watch against the lightening sky.

choices.description: I will send the Delivery Boy to the counter to hold the bell while we finish on the veranda.

line.dialogue: I see the boy sprint off along the planks.
I watch the boy hesitate, unsure which platform.

choices.description: I will draft the death entry here, in my best formal hand, for the Officer to copy into the register.

line.dialogue: I see him read my draft and nod once.
I see him close my notebook gently and take out his own.

lines.dialogue: First light at the rice counter; farmers queue with sacks; the ledger waits under its lacquered lid, rice grains pressed between its pages.
Order travels. It is the one thing from home that does.
lines.stage_directions: sets out the file case, the death register, his own ink block, a folding rule, the bell-rope tag — each in its place

lines.dialogue: My boy always took the other side.
lines.stage_directions: grips the sack's single handle

lines.dialogue: A young farmer steps out of the queue.
Let me try — wanna try it together, uncle?
The bell rings when the sack is weighed. Unrung, the tally waits. But the register of the dead cannot wait past dawn prayers.
Stop. Not yet.
lines.stage_directions: raises his hand toward the bell

lines.dialogue: Then we choose the order of the books.
lines.stage_directions: to Phum

lines.dialogue: The queue holds its breath above the platform.

line.dialogue: The bell or the book, teacher. Which does my boy get first?

choices.description: I will ask the Officer to write the death entry first, before any weighing.

line.dialogue: I see the Officer open the register to the names of the dead.
I see him touch the bell-rope tag instead.

choices.description: I will lift the sack's second handle myself so the weighing can wait.

line.dialogue: I feel the sack rise between us, steady.
I feel the handle slip and the grain shift inside.

choices.description: I will propose the tally record the field 'one hand short' so next season's rate is argued now, in writing.

line.dialogue: I see the Officer rule a new column in the ledger.
I see him shake his head at the lacquered lid.

lines.dialogue: The sack rises between two men; the brass scale settles; the bell stays quiet in the Officer's hand.
Birth. Marriage. Death. Tax. The capital prints a line for each — and no line for what the dead still do. His hand is in this harvest.
lines.stage_directions: writes the death entry slowly, checking each letter

lines.dialogue: One book, four columns. It is not enough paper.
lines.stage_directions: touches each form in the register in turn

lines.dialogue: This harvest — I did it all myself. And it weighs short.
lines.stage_directions: watches the scale

lines.dialogue: The scale reads two baskets under the tally.
Move a bit further from the platform, please. A bit further.
lines.stage_directions: to the pressing queue

lines.dialogue: Two baskets.
lines.stage_directions: reads the scale over the Officer's shoulder

lines.dialogue: The scale says one thing. The field would have given another.
lines.stage_directions: pen above the page

line.dialogue: Two baskets short. Do I write the weight the scale says, or the weight the field would have given?

choices.description: I will tell him to write the scale's weight — a register of lies feeds no one.

line.dialogue: I see him write the true number and ring the bell once.
I see him hold the pen above the page.

choices.description: I will offer the school's rice store to make up the two baskets on paper.

line.dialogue: I see him note the school's seal beside the entry.
I see him wave it off — the state counts sacks, not kindness.

choices.description: I will argue that the son's name stays on the field's line until the harvest he planted is sold.

line.dialogue: I see him write both names, the living above the dead.
I see him strike the second name out.

acts.title: The Line the Capital Didn't Print

lines.dialogue: Full morning on the veranda; the bell's single note still hangs over the water; the register is closed.
I am exact because exactness travels well. Home does not.
lines.stage_directions: drinks tea, the file case shut at his feet

lines.dialogue: Exactness is a poor traveler but a good guest.
lines.stage_directions: pours him more tea

lines.dialogue: My posting ends with the rains. I'm leaving soon.
lines.stage_directions: looks at the rain-clouds

lines.dialogue: Not the state's register. Ours. We keep names here for reading aloud.
lines.stage_directions: opens the school's own book and writes the boy's name

lines.dialogue: Some mornings the register makes me feel — uncomfortable.
lines.stage_directions: turns the register's cover without opening it

lines.dialogue: The circle settles; the pond takes the light.
For the school's store. From the short field.
lines.stage_directions: sets a small sack of rice at Lek's feet

lines.dialogue: Teacher. The forms have no line for the dead who still work.
lines.stage_directions: takes up the register at last

line.dialogue: The forms have no line for the dead who still work. Do I leave the page as the capital printed it, or do you rule me a new line?

choices.description: I will rule him a new line in the school's book only.

line.dialogue: I see him copy the heading in his exact hand.
I see him smile and say one book is burden enough.

choices.description: I will propose the veranda witness such entries each quarter moon.

line.dialogue: I see him note the next quarter moon in his register margin.
I see him close the register on the idea.

choices.description: I will dare him to write the new line into the state's own register, initials small.

line.dialogue: I see him write the heading, initials small beneath.
I see him lock the file case on the register.
